title: Tran dynasty
capsule: The Trần dynasty (Nhà Trần) ruled Đại Việt from 1226 to 1400, replacing the Lý dynasty when Trần Thủ Độ engineered the marriage of the last Lý child-empress to Trần Cảnh, the first Trần emperor (Trần Thái Tông, r. 1226–1258). The dynasty's defining achievement was the repulsion of three Mongol-Yuan invasions in 1258, 1285, and 1288; the 1288 victory on the Bạch Đằng River, organized by general Trần Hưng Đạo, stands as one of the most celebrated military feats in Vietnamese history. After the death of Trần Hưng Đạo in 1300 the dynasty progressively weakened under Cham pressure from the south and internal factional conflict; in 1400 the regent Hồ Quý Ly deposed the last Trần emperor and founded the Hồ dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territorial extent of Đại Việt under Trần rule is reasonably well attested through Vietnamese chronicles (Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư); the precise southern frontier with Champa fluctuated with military campaigns and is not mapped exactly.
